subject.title: Browser-heavy sessions block all main lanes — need dedicated browser lane or per-channel lane routing

question: Should OpenClaw add public lane-routing semantics for browser/workload/channel isolation, and should that contract be browser-only, per-channel, per-agent, workload-classified, or priority-based?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public scheduler/config semantics and must settle compatibility, resource caps, trust boundaries, and overlap with adjacent lane proposals.

options.title: Design a unified scheduler lane model
options.body: Add a server-owned lane classification contract covering slow workloads and channel/agent isolation with aggregate caps, docs, schema, and migration expectations before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to browser-only isolation
options.body: Implement a smaller browser workload lane if maintainers decide browser automation is the only supported special case for now.

options.title: Fold into broader per-agent scheduler work
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43235 as the design vehicle and keep this issue as browser/workload evidence rather than adding a separate API.

recommendation.title: Design a unified scheduler lane model
recommendation.body: Add a server-owned lane classification contract covering slow workloads and channel/agent isolation with aggregate caps, docs, schema, and migration expectations before implementation.
